story: Joan Miró authored the original poetry and produced the color lithographs for the illustrated book project titled Le Lézard aux plumes d'or. In 1967, he executed a series of lithographs to accompany the poem, but for technical reasons, he chose to destroy those initial prints. He reworked the project and saw it through to completion when publisher Louis Broder issued the finished edition in Paris in 1971.

In 1971, publisher Louis Broder brought Joan Miró's Le Lézard aux plumes d'or to fruition in Paris. The artist created fifteen color lithographs to accompany a series of his own poems. The plates were printed directly at the Mourlot workshop, pairing Miró's text with original lithographic prints on paper.

In 1967, Joan Miró created a series of color lithographs to illustrate his own poetry for the book project *Le Lézard aux plumes d'or*. The plates were printed in Paris at Atelier Mourlot under the direction of the publisher Louis Broder. Although an initial suite of lithographs was produced that year, Miró ultimately decided to destroy the run for technical reasons. The finalized edition of the illustrated book was subsequently printed and published in 1971.
